[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for taking time today. Quick intro: I'm Alex Chen, AE, and with me are Maya, our solutions eng, and Jordan from CSM.
[00:08] Priya (SummitWorks): Hi Alex, thanks. We have Leah and Ethan here as well. We're trying to run procurement gating this week.
[00:15] Maya (Redwood SE): Hey, quick note, happy to dig into KMS and private deployment notes — we'll try not to get too deep yet but can.
[00:21] Leah (Legal): Great. Primary asks: MSA redlines, data processing additions in the DPA for EU customers, and clarity on SLA credits.
[00:30] Alex: Totally. High level: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), and Private (VPC / on-prem). For procurement you folks usually choose Dedicated or Private for regulated workloads.
[00:44] Ethan: Can you explain the KMS options again? We need to know whether keys are customer managed or Redwood-managed if we do Private.
[00:52] Maya: Sure — we support multiple patterns. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) with HSM-backed providers; for Dedicated we can do either RBAC with keys in your cloud KMS or a tenant-specific HSM path in private deployments. Note: the K V cache — sorry K V (KV) cache — does not store plaintext keys.
[01:15] Leah: There was a previous doc that said 'custody of keys' and it read ambiguous, legal flagged it.
[01:22] Alex: We'll surface clear language. We'll send a short technical appendix describing custody, encryption-at-rest, in-transit, and the exact KMS call flow.
[01:29] Priya: On pricing, procurement wants to see: reserved capacity pricing for 3 and 12-month commits, and egress scenarios — we have heavy EU traffic.
[01:38] Alex: Understood. For reserved capacity we do monthly committed GPUs with overage billing. We can show blended per-token math for your baseline plus tail traffic. We'll include an egress sensitivity sheet.
[01:47] Ethan: SLA — we need explicit p99 latency windows for text-generation calls; is that covered in Dedicated?
[01:55] Maya: Yes, Dedicated has SLA targets we can map to p95/p99 for specific model families. For Hosted we offer best-effort with SLOs; Dedicated and Private are where you get contractual latency targets and credits. There is nuance: sequence length and KV cache hit rate affect p99.
[02:13] Leah: About credits: legal wants a cap on credits and a clear calculation formula, not open-ended damage language.
[02:20] Alex: We can propose standard credit formulas — percentage of fees for the affected month, capped at X% of monthly fees. We'll propose something that procurement typically accepts.
[02:30] Priya: Timeline — we need vendor accepted and signed by end of month ideally. Is that realistic?
[02:35] Jordan (CSM): If we get redlines this week we can often compress review cycles. The critical path is Legal review and procurement acceptance.
[02:43] Leah: We'll try. One other thing: data residency for EU — the DPA needs to specify that EU customer data stays in EU region and not replicated to US without controls.
[02:54] Maya: For Private/VPC you control region. For Hosted we have regional endpoints; we can add binding commitments in the DPA for region-specific processing and egress. We'll flag cross-border transfer clauses and subprocessors list.
[03:10] Ethan: What about audit logs and traceability? We need immutable audit logs and token-level reporting.
[03:17] Alex: Redwood Console offers token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and you can export audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 push. We'll include sample retention options and pricing for longer retention in the security pack.
[03:31] Priya: Is there a SOC2 report we can review?
[03:34] Jordan: Yes, SOC2 Type II available. We'll include the report and a summary of the scope. Also ISO 27001 snapshot and pen-test exec summary.
[03:44] Leah: For MSA redlines — main items are: limitation of liability caps, indemnity carveouts, data handling representations, and subprocessor list.
[03:54] Alex: We expect some negotiation on those. We'll send an annotated MSA that highlights suggested language and where we can be flexible vs where we need to keep standard terms (insurance, indemnity, export controls).
[04:05] Priya: Pricing objections we expect from finance: the per-token model vs flat committed throughput. They want a deterministic bill.
[04:13] Maya: Many customers blend both — reserved capacity for baseline traffic (predictable bill) and pay-as-you-go for bursts. We'll model a blended rate so you can see per-transaction cost under different utilization.
[04:25] Ethan: Latency vs cost tradeoff — if we target 50ms p99 are we looking at a material price premium?
[04:31] Maya: Yes, lower latency targets push toward dedicated capacity and hotter kernels / GPU families; there's a delta. We'll show sample delta on the pricing sheet. Also quantization and batching changes quality/latency tradeoffs.
[04:46] Leah: We also have security requirements re: privileged access for debug sessions. We need an ability to audit and require two-person access for specific actions.
[04:56] Maya: For Private and Dedicated we can implement role-based access controls and require multi-person approval for key rotation or escalated access. We'll outline the RBAC model and audit hooks.
[05:10] Priya: For the DPA, who is the subprocessor list? We need names for cloud providers and any analytics vendors.
[05:17] Alex: We'll include a current subprocessor list, and a commitment to notify you of changes within X days.
[05:23] Leah: On export controls, we need assurance that data subject to export restrictions is handled properly.
[05:28] Maya: We'll add a clause and map our subprocessors and regions. For private on-prem deployments, export-control risk is minimal since it stays on-prem.
[05:37] Priya: Can you give an example of the pilot SLA and success metrics?
[05:41] Jordan: Typical pilot: 30 days, defined prompts and eval set, target p95 latency < 300ms and accuracy/quality thresholds on the eval prompts. If we miss the SLA by more than threshold, credits or extended pilot at no cost.
[05:56] Ethan: We might ask for an on-prem PoC instead of Hosted for initial compliance checks. How long to stand up Private?
[06:02] Maya: Private can be weeks-to-months depending on networking and access approvals; Dedicated is faster — we can provision reserved pools in cloud regions in days, but Private with on-prem appliance takes longer. We'll put an estimated timeline in the SOW.
[06:18] Priya: Procurement will want acceptance criteria for onboarding; can you share a checklist?
[06:22] Jordan: Yes, we'll share the onboarding checklist and required network configurations (egress rules, ports, certs).
[06:28] Leah: About the credit formula again — we want specific math in the SLA, with examples.
[06:33] Alex: We'll include worked examples: if p99 > target for > 3 days, credit = X% of monthly fee times days missed, capped at Y% of monthly fee.
[06:44] Priya: Ok. Anything else from Redwood side?
[06:48] Maya: Two items: 1) a technical note on inference determinism and tokenization mismatches — we will show model family-specific behaviors; 2) an ops runbook for failure modes and fallbacks, e.g., routing to smaller model when big one hits capacity.
[07:05] Ethan: Good, ops runbook would help our SREs.
[07:08] Leah: On the MSA, we may request a higher-capped liability for specific data classes — is that negotiable?
[07:15] Alex: We can talk about tiered liability for regulated data; often we trade that for higher insurance coverage. We'll note that in the redline summary.
[07:26] Priya: Let's talk schedule: we'll aim to circulate redlines by Friday. Can you commit to sending the annotated MSA and DPA by tomorrow?
[07:33] Alex: Yes, we will send annotated MSA/DPA and a short exceptions tracker by EOD 2025-06-10.
[07:39] Jordan: And I'll attach the pilot SOW and onboarding checklist in that email.
[07:45] Leah: Great. One small point — we have an existing SSO provider, Okta; need SAML metadata exchange info.
[07:51] Maya: We support Okta SAML and OIDC. We'll include the SAML metadata template and example claims mapping.
[07:58] Priya: Any competitor-specific questions? Procurement asked if you integrate with VendorX billing connectors.
[08:03] Alex: We don't have an out-of-the-box connector for VendorX billing; we can export billing CSVs and integrate via your finops pipeline.
[08:12] Ethan: Are there any penalties for early contract termination on reserved capacity?
[08:17] Alex: There are typically pro-rata exit terms for reserved commitments; we'll surface exact language in the MSA sample.
[08:24] Leah: We also require proof of cyber insurance and certificate — can you provide your carrier and coverage limits?
[08:29] Jordan: We'll include summary and certificate of insurance in the security pack.
[08:34] Priya: Ok this is useful. Anything else from customer side?
[08:38] Ethan: We'll want a short technical deep-dive after legal sign-off to hammer out KMS integration details.
[08:44] Alex: Sounds good. We'll propose two meetings: one legal redline call (legal + procurement) and one technical deep-dive (SRE + SE).
[08:52] Leah: We'll pick dates after internal alignment.
[08:55] Alex: Quick recap: Redwood sends annotated MSA/DPA + security pack + pricing worksheets + SOW and onboarding checklist. Customer to send redlines by 2025-06-13. Follow-up legal call week of 2025-06-16.
